# LNAV -- The Logfile Navigator

The Logfile Navigator is a log file viewer for the terminal. Given a
set of files/directories, **lnav** will:

- decompress as needed;
- detect their format;
- merge the files by time into a single view;
- tail the files, follow renames, find new files in directories;
- build an index of errors and warnings;
- pretty-print JSON-lines.

Then, in the **lnav** TUI, you can:

- jump quickly to the previous/next error (press `e`/`E`);
- search using regular expressions (press `/`);
- highlight text with a regular expression (`:highlight` command);
- filter messages using regular expressions or SQLite expressions;
- pretty-print structured text (press `P`);
- view a histogram of messages over time (press `i`);
- analyze messages using SQLite (press `;`)

## Screenshot

The following screenshot shows a mix of syslog and web access log
files. Failed requests are shown in red. Identifiers, like IP
address and PIDs are semantically highlighted.

[![Screenshot](https://lnav.org/assets/images/lnav-front-page.png)](https://lnav.org/assets/images/lnav-front-page.png)

## Why not **just** use `tail`/`grep`/`less`?

The standard Unix utilities are great for processing raw text lines,
however, they do not understand log messages. Tail can watch
multiple files at a time, but it won't display messages in order by
time and you can't scroll backwards. Grep will only find matching
lines, but won't return a full multi-line log message. Less can only
display a single file at a time. Also, none of these basic tools
handle compressed files.

## Try online before installing

You can SSH into a demo node to play with lnav before installing.

The "playground" account starts lnav with a couple of log files as
an example:

`$ ssh playground@demo.lnav.org`

The "tutorial 1" account is an interactive tutorial that can teach
you the basics of operation:

`$ ssh tutorial1@demo.lnav.org`

## Installation

Download a statically-linked binary for Linux/MacOS/Windows from the release page:
https://github.com/tstack/lnav/releases/latest

### Brew on MacOS

```console
$ brew install lnav
```

## Usage

Simply point **lnav** at the files or directories you want to
monitor, it will figure out the rest:

```console
$ lnav /path/to/file1 /path/to/dir ...
```

The **lnav** TUI will pop up right away and begin indexing the
files. Progress is displayed in the "Files" panel at the
bottom. Once the indexing has finished, the LOG view will display
the log messages that were recognized. You can then use the
usual hotkeys to move around the view (arrow keys or
`j`/`k`/`h`/`l` to move down/up/left/right).

Files that do not contain log messages can be seen in the
TEXT view (reachable by pressing `t`).

### Usage with `systemd-journald`

On systems running `systemd-journald`, you can use `lnav` as the pager:

```
$ journalctl | lnav
```

or in follow mode:

```
$ journalctl -f | lnav
```

Since `journalctl`'s default output format omits the year, if you are
viewing logs which span multiple years you will need to change the
output format to include the year, otherwise `lnav` gets confused:

```
$ journalctl -o short-iso | lnav
```

It is also possible to use `journalctl`'s json output format and `lnav`
will make use of additional fields such as PRIORITY and \_SYSTEMD_UNIT:

```
$ journalctl -o json | lnav
```

In case some MESSAGE fields contain special characters such as
ANSI color codes which are considered as unprintable by journalctl,
specifying `journalctl`'s `-a` option might be preferable in order
to output those messages still in a non-binary representation:

```
$ journalctl -a -o json | lnav
```

If using systemd v236 or newer, the output fields can be limited to
the ones actually recognized by `lnav` for increased efficiency:

```
$ journalctl -o json --output-fields=MESSAGE,PRIORITY,_PID,SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER,_SYSTEMD_UNIT | lnav
```

If your system has been running for a long time, for increased
efficiency you may want to limit the number of log lines fed into
`lnav`, e.g. via `journalctl`'s `-n` or `--since=...` options.

In case of a persistent journal, you may want to limit the number
of log lines fed into `lnav` via `journalctl`'s `-b` option.

## Support

Please file issues on this repository or use the discussions section.
The following alternatives are also available:

- support@lnav.org
- Discord: https://discord.gg/erBPnKwz7R
- Google Groups: https://groups.google.com/g/lnav

## Links

- Main Site: https://lnav.org
- Documentation: https://docs.lnav.org

lnav \- log file viewer for the terminal
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B lnav 
[options] [logfile1 logfile2 ...]
.SH DESCRIPTION
The Logfile Navigator, lnav, is a log file viewer for the terminal.
Given a set of files/directories, lnav will:
.TP
- decompress as needed;
.TP
- detect their format;
.TP
- merge the files together by time into a single view;
.TP
- tail the files, follow renames, find new files in directories;
.TP
- build an index of errors and warnings;
.TP
- pretty-print JSON-lines.
.SH KEY BINDINGS
.TP
?
View/leave the online help text.
.TP
q
Quit the program.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR
Print help and exit
.TP
\fB\-H\fR
Display the internal help text.
.TP
\fB\-I\fR path
Add the given configuration directory to the search path.
.TP
\fB\-W\fR
Print warnings related to lnav's configuration.
.TP
\fB\-u\fR
Update formats installed from git repositories.
.TP
\fB\-d\fR file
Write debug messages to the given file.
.TP
\fB\-V\fR
Print version information.
.TP
\fB\-r\fR
Recursively load files from the given directories.
.TP
\fB\-R\fR
Load older rotated log files as well.
.TP
\fB\-c\fR cmd
Execute a command after the files have been loaded.
.TP
\fB\-f\fR path
Execute the commands in the given file.
.TP
\fB\-e\fR cmd
Execute a shell command-line.
.TP
\fB\-t\fR
Prepend timestamps to the lines of data being read in
on the standard input.
.TP
\fB\-n\fR
Run without the curses UI.  (headless mode)
.TP
\fB\-N\fR
Do not open the default syslog file if no files are given.
.TP
\fB\-q\fR
Quiet mode.  Do not print the log messages after executing all of the commands.
.SS "Optional arguments:"
.TP
logfile1
The log files or directories to view.  If a
directory is given, all of the files in the
directory will be loaded.
.SH MANAGEMENT-MODE OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-i\fR
Install the given format files in the $HOME/.lnav/formats/installed directory
and exit.
.TP
\fB\-m\fR
Switch to the management command-line mode.  This mode is
used to work with lnav's configuration.
.TP
\fB\-C\fR
Check the configuration and exit.  The log format files will be loaded and
checked.  Any files given on the command-line will be loaded checked to make
sure they match a log format.
.SH EXAMPLES
To load and follow the syslog file:
.PP
.Vb 1
\&    lnav
.Ve
.PP
To load all of the files in /var/log:
.PP
.Vb 1
\&    lnav /var/log
.Ve
.PP
To watch the output of make with timestamps prepended:
.PP
.Vb 1
\&    make 2>&1 | lnav \-t
.Ve

lnav 0.14.0

A fancy log file viewer for the terminal.

Overview

The Logfile Navigator, lnav, is an enhanced log file viewer that takes
advantage of any semantic information that can be gleaned from the
files being viewed, such as timestamps and log levels. Using this
extra semantic information, lnav can do things like interleaving
messages from different files, generate histograms of messages over
time, and providing hotkeys for navigating through the file. It is
hoped that these features will allow the user to quickly and
efficiently zero in on problems.

Opening Paths/URLs

The main arguments to lnav are the local/remote files, directories,
glob patterns, or URLs to be viewed. If no arguments are given, the
default syslog file for your system will be opened. These arguments
will be polled periodically so that any new data or files will be
automatically loaded. If a previously loaded file is removed or
replaced, it will be closed and the replacement opened.

Note: When opening SFTP URLs, if the password is not provided for the
host, the SSH agent can be used to do authentication.

Options

Lnav takes a list of files to view and/or you can use the flag
arguments to load well-known log files, such as the syslog log files.
The flag arguments are:

 •  -r  Recursively load files from the given directory
   hierarchies.
 •  -R  Load older rotated log files as well.

When using the flag arguments, lnav will look for the files relative
to the current directory and its parent directories. In other words,
if you are working within a directory that has the well-known log
files, those will be preferred over any others.

If you do not want the default syslog file to be loaded when no files
are specified, you can pass the  -N  flag.

Any files given on the command-line are scanned to determine their log
file format and to create an index for each line in the file. You do
not have to manually specify the log file format. The currently
supported formats are: syslog, apache, strace, tcsh history, and
generic log files with timestamps.

Lnav will also display data piped in on the standard input.

To automatically execute queries or lnav commands after the files have
been loaded, you can use the following options:

 •  -c cmd  A command, query, or file to execute. The
   first character determines the type of operation: a colon
   ( : ) is used for the built-in commands; a semi-colon (
    ; ) for SQL/PRQL queries; and a pipe symbol ( | ) for
   executing a file containing other commands. For example,
   to open the file "foo.log" and go to the tenth line in
   the file, you can do:
   
    ▌lnav -c ':goto 10' foo.log              
   
   This option can be given multiple times to execute
   multiple operations in sequence.
 •  -f file  A file that contains commands, queries, or
   files to execute. This option is a shortcut for
    -c '|file' . You can use a dash ( - ) to execute
   commands from the standard input.

To execute commands/queries without opening the interactive text UI,
you can pass the  -n  option. This combination of options allows you
to write scripts for processing logs with lnav. For example, to get a
list of IP addresses that dhclient has bound to in CSV format:

#!/bin/sh

IN_PID=`cat`

if test "${IN_PID}" -gt 0 > /dev/null 2>&1 && \
    kill -0 $IN_PID > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "== ps =="
    ps uewww -p $IN_PID
    echo "== lsof =="
    lsof -p $IN_PID
else
    echo "error: inaccessible process -- $IN_PID" > /dev/stderr
fi
#
# @synopsis: rename-stdin <name>
# @description: Give a symbolic name to the standard-input file
#

;SELECT raise_error('expecting the new name for stdin as the first argument') WHERE $1 IS NULL
;SELECT raise_error('no data was redirected to lnav''s standard-input')
        WHERE (SELECT count(1) FROM lnav_file WHERE filepath='stdin') = 0

;UPDATE lnav_file SET filepath=$1 WHERE filepath='stdin'

;SELECT 'info: renamed stdin to ' || $1 AS msg
#
# @synopsis: dhclient-summary
# @description: Generate a summary of DHCP addresses bound in this log
#

:echo DHCP leases over time:
:echo
;SELECT ip AS IP, start_time AS "Start Time",
        printf("% 24s", CASE
          WHEN end_time IS NULL THEN printf("%s%s%s", $ansi_green, 'Active', $ansi_norm)
          ELSE
          printf("%s%.02f%s hours", $ansi_bold, (julianday(end_time) - julianday(start_time)) * 24, $ansi_norm)
        END) AS Duration
  FROM
  (WITH lease_times AS
    (SELECT min(log_time) AS start_time, ip FROM
      (SELECT log_time, regexp_match('bound to (\S+) --', log_text) AS ip FROM syslog_log WHERE ip IS NOT NULL)
     GROUP BY ip ORDER BY start_time ASC)
    SELECT start_time,
           (SELECT lt2.start_time AS end_time FROM lease_times AS lt2 WHERE lt1.start_time < lt2.start_time LIMIT 1) AS end_time,
           ip
      FROM lease_times AS lt1)

lnav 0.14.0

A fancy log file viewer for the terminal.

Overview

The Logfile Navigator, lnav, is an enhanced log file viewer that takes
advantage of any semantic information that can be gleaned from the
files being viewed, such as timestamps and log levels. Using this
extra semantic information, lnav can do things like interleaving
messages from different files, generate histograms of messages over
time, and providing hotkeys for navigating through the file. It is
hoped that these features will allow the user to quickly and
efficiently zero in on problems.

Opening Paths/URLs

The main arguments to lnav are the local/remote files, directories,
glob patterns, or URLs to be viewed. If no arguments are given, the
default syslog file for your system will be opened. These arguments
will be polled periodically so that any new data or files will be
automatically loaded. If a previously loaded file is removed or
replaced, it will be closed and the replacement opened.

Note: When opening SFTP URLs, if the password is not provided for the
host, the SSH agent can be used to do authentication.

Options

Lnav takes a list of files to view and/or you can use the flag
arguments to load well-known log files, such as the syslog log files.
The flag arguments are:

 •  -r  Recursively load files from the given directory
   hierarchies.
 •  -R  Load older rotated log files as well.

When using the flag arguments, lnav will look for the files relative
to the current directory and its parent directories. In other words,
if you are working within a directory that has the well-known log
files, those will be preferred over any others.

If you do not want the default syslog file to be loaded when no files
are specified, you can pass the  -N  flag.

Any files given on the command-line are scanned to determine their log
file format and to create an index for each line in the file. You do
not have to manually specify the log file format. The currently
supported formats are: syslog, apache, strace, tcsh history, and
generic log files with timestamps.

Lnav will also display data piped in on the standard input.

To automatically execute queries or lnav commands after the files have
been loaded, you can use the following options:

 •  -c cmd  A command, query, or file to execute. The

    ; ) for SQL/PRQL queries; and a pipe symbol ( | ) for

  syslog_version  INTEGER  COLLATE 'BINARY'       , -- The version of the syslog format used for this message

  -- END Format-specific fields

  log_mark         BOOLEAN,                           -- True if the log message was marked
  log_sticky_mark  BOOLEAN HIDDEN,                    -- True if the log message is a sticky header
  log_comment      TEXT,                              -- The comment for this message
  log_tags         TEXT,                              -- A JSON list of tags for this message
  log_annotations  TEXT,                              -- A JSON object of annotations for this messages
  log_filters      TEXT,                              -- A JSON list of filter IDs that matched this message
  log_opid         TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The message's OPID from the log message or user
  log_user_opid    TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The message's OPID as set by the user
  log_opid_definition TEXT HIDDEN,                    -- The matching OPID description definition
  log_format       TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The name of the log file format
  log_format_regex TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The name of the regex used to parse this log message

  log_path         TEXT HIDDEN COLLATE naturalnocase, -- The path to the log file this message is from
  log_unique_path  TEXT HIDDEN COLLATE naturalnocase, -- The unique portion of the path this message is from
  log_text         TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The full text of the log message
  log_body         TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The body of the log message

  log_thread_id    TEXT HIDDEN,                       -- The ID of the thread that generated this message
  log_duration     REAL HIDDEN                        -- The duration associated with this log message
, PRIMARY KEY (log_line)
);

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Session command execution (attached as methods)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _sess_exec_sql(self, sql_text, orig_cmd):
    sql_stripped = sql_text.strip()
    # .schema special case: SQL text after ';' whose stripped form starts with '.schema'
    if sql_stripped.startswith(".schema"):
        self.write_out(data_text("schema.txt", ""))
        # Does .schema change view/last_query? It prints directly; subsequent default print
        # would duplicate if we also set last_query. Observed: '; .schema' alone prints schema once.
        # Mark a flag to suppress default output? Our driver prints default output at end unless suppressed.
        # Reference behavior with -q / with files + .schema unknown; suppress default by setting view to schema?
        # Simpler: set a flag _wrote_direct and change current view lines to empty? We'll set last_query=None and
        # view_stack top to 'schema' would print schema again in default. Instead set flag.
        self._direct_output_done = True
        return
    # Expand $ENV / $1 params: sqlite supports $VAR as named params - Python sqlite does NOT support $VAR syntax
    # in the same way? It supports :name and ? but $name is also supported by SQLite C API - python's sqlite3
    # passes through to C, so $HOME would be a parameter needing binding. We'll translate:
    # $VAR -> env value param, $1 -> script arg / NULL, :foo -> NULL (unless focused-msg col in scripts)
    # Keep column-name translation for execute: replace $... and :name outside string literals with ? params.
    # This is approximate; string literals containing $ are rare in tests.
    params = []
    def _param_for(var):
        if var.isdigit():
            idx = int(var)
            if self.script_args and 1 <= idx <= len(self.script_args):
                v = self.script_args[idx - 1]
                # Script args that look numeric? Keep as text; sqlite affinity handles.
                params.append(v)
            else:
                params.append(None)
        elif var in os.environ:
            params.append(os.environ[var])
        elif var.startswith("ansi_"):
            ansi = {"ansi_green": "\x1b[32m", "ansi_norm": "\x1b[0m", "ansi_bold": "\x1b[1m",
                    "ansi_red": "\x1b[31m", "ansi_yellow": "\x1b[33m"}
            params.append(ansi.get(var, ""))
        else:
            # Could be a :log_body style reference in session scripts - bind NULL
            params.append(None)
        return "?"
    # Split by string literals to avoid replacing inside quotes
    parts = re.split(r"('(?:[^']|'')*')", sql_text)
    new_parts = []
    for part in parts:
        if part.startswith("'"):
            new_parts.append(part)
        else:
            # $VAR or $1
            part = re.sub(r"\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*|\d+)", lambda m: _param_for(m.group(1)), part)
            # :name params (but not :: or time 'HH:MM' inside? already outside quotes; times in SQL would be quoted)
            part = re.sub(r":([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", lambda m: _param_for(m.group(1)), part)
            new_parts.append(part)
    exec_sql = "".join(new_parts)
    self._raise_error_msg = None
    try:
        cur = self.db.cursor()
        cur.execute(exec_sql, params)
        if cur.description is not None:
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            rows = cur.fetchall()
            # Special: PRAGMA table_info needs hidden/type/pk matching reference, not sqlite's.
            pm = re.match(r"\s*PRAGMA\s+table_info\s*\(\s*'?\"?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\"?'?\s*\)", sql_text, re.I)
            if pm:
                cols, rows = pragma_table_info(self, pm.group(1))
            # Tables like regexp_capture('..','..') / fstat('..') are table-valued functions - handle before?
            self.last_query = (cols, rows)
            if self.current_view() != "db":
                self.view_stack.append("db")
            self._populate_views()
        else:
            # INSERT/UPDATE etc. Reference: output empty, view? INSERT INTO lnav_example_log gave no output and no db view print.
            # Check if statement is SELECT-like with no description? Keep last_query unchanged, don't switch view.
            # Detect message-style SELECT results: e.g. scripts do ;SELECT 'info: ...' AS msg expecting? rename-stdin script ends with that.
            # But our cur.description would be non-None for SELECT. For UPDATE lnav_file etc, apply side effects:
            self._handle_sql_side_effects(sql_text, exec_sql, params)
            try:
                self.db.commit()
            except Exception:
                pass
    except Exception as e:
        if getattr(self, "_raise_error_msg", None) is not None:
            self.write_err(f"  error: {self._raise_error_msg}\n --> {self.cmd_source}:{self.cmd_index}\n | {pad_cmd_line(orig_cmd)}\n")
            return
        # Table-valued functions fallback: regexp_capture / fstat / xpath
        handled = self._try_table_valued(sql_text, orig_cmd)
        if handled:
            return
        msg = str(e)
        # Normalize some messages to reference wording
        # sqlite python messages are same C messages mostly: 'no such table: foo', 'near "SELEC": syntax error'
        self.write_err(
            f"  error: failed to compile SQL statement\n reason: {msg}\n"
            f" --> {self.cmd_source}:{self.cmd_index}\n | {pad_cmd_line(sql_text.strip())}\n")
        # On SQL error, reference suppresses default view print (OUT empty). Achieve by flag.
        self._sql_error = True
        self._direct_output_done = True  # suppress default print? But multiple commands: later commands may still print.
        # Actually for ";SELECT * FROM foo" with file, OUT was '' (default suppressed). For simplicity suppress if this was last?
        # We'll let driver decide: if any error occurred and view is log, still print? Probe: mark-expr error + write error -> OUT ''.
        # :goto abc error -> OUT ''. So errors generally suppress default output. Track _had_error.
        self._had_error = True

def pragma_table_info(sess, tname):
    # Return reference-style pragma rows
    schema_text = data_text("schema.txt", "")
    tables = parse_schema_columns(schema_text)
    simple = parse_simple_tables(schema_text)
    cols_def = tables.get(tname) or simple.get(tname)
    if cols_def is None:
        # fallback to sqlite pragma
        try:
            cur = sess.db.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({tname})")
            rows = cur.fetchall()
            return ([d[0] for d in cur.description], rows)
        except Exception:
            return (["cid", "name", "type", "notnull", "dflt_value", "pk"], [])
    rows = []
    for i, (col, typ, hidden, pk) in enumerate(cols_def):
        # Visible + hidden interleaved as in schema order; reference PRAGMA truncates after visible+
        # some hidden? Observed syslog PRAGMA output continued past log_annotations (hidden cols follow).
        # Our earlier probe truncated display at 4000 chars, not actual. Include all.
        rows.append((i, col, typ, 0, None, pk))
    return (["cid", "name", "type", "notnull", "dflt_value", "pk"], rows)

def _sess_handle_sql_side_effects(self, OrigSql, exec_sql, params):
    # UPDATE lnav_file SET filepath=... (rename-stdin)
    m = re.match(r"\s*UPDATE\s+lnav_file\s+SET\s+filepath\s*=\s*\?\s+WHERE\s+filepath\s*=\s*'stdin'", exec_sql, re.I)
    if m and params:
        newname = params[0]
        for lf in self.files:
            if lf.filepath == "stdin":
                lf.filepath = str(newname)
        for msg in self.messages:
            if msg.path == "stdin":
                msg.path = str(newname)
        self._populate_db()
    # UPDATE on log tables for log_mark etc: our DB tables are copies; re-sync marks if possible (skip)

def _sess_try_table_valued(self, sql_text, orig_cmd):
    s = sql_text.strip()
    # SELECT * FROM regexp_capture('str', 'pat') [... WHERE etc not supported fully]
    m = re.search(r"regexp_capture\s*\(\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*,\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*\)", s)
    kind = None
    if "regexp_capture(" in s or "regexp_capture_into_json(" in s:
        kind = "regexp_capture"
    elif re.search(r"\bfstat\s*\(", s):
        kind = "fstat"
    if kind == "regexp_capture" and m:
        hay = m.group(1).replace("''", "'")
        pat = m.group(2).replace("''", "'")
        try:
            rx = re.compile(_convert_pattern(pat))
        except Exception:
            return False
        cols = ["match_index", "capture_index", "capture_name", "capture_count", "range_start", "range_stop", "content"]
        rows = []
        for mi, mm in enumerate(rx.finditer(hay)):
            groups = [mm.group(0)] + list(mm.groups())
            spans = [mm.span(0)] + [mm.span(i + 1) for i in range(len(mm.groups()))]
            names = [None]
            inv = {v: k for k, v in rx.groupindex.items()}
            for gi in range(len(mm.groups())):
                names.append(inv.get(gi + 1))
            for ci, (content, (a, b)) in enumerate(zip(groups, spans)):
                rows.append((mi, ci, names[ci] if ci < len(names) else None, len(groups), a + 1, b + 1, content))
        self.last_query = (cols, rows)
        if self.current_view() != "db":
            self.view_stack.append("db")
        self._had_error = False
        self._direct_output_done = False
        return True
    if kind == "fstat":
        m2 = re.search(r"fstat\s*\(\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*\)", s)
        if not m2:
            return False
        path = m2.group(1).replace("''", "'")
        cols = ["st_parent", "st_name", "st_dev", "st_ino", "st_type", "st_mode", "st_nlink",
                "st_uid", "st_user", "st_gid", "st_group", "st_rdev", "st_size", "st_blksize",
                "st_blocks", "st_atime", "st_mtime", "st_ctime", "error"]
        try:
            import pwd, grp
            st = os.stat(path)
            parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)) + "/"
            name = os.path.basename(path)
            typ = "reg" if os.path.isfile(path) else ("dir" if os.path.isdir(path) else "unknown")
            try:
                user = pwd.getpwuid(st.st_uid).pw_name
            except Exception:
                user = str(st.st_uid)
            try:
                group = grp.getgrgid(st.st_gid).gr_name
            except Exception:
                group = str(st.st_gid)
            def ftime(t):
                dt = datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(t)
                return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.") + f"{dt.microsecond:06d}"
            row = (parent, name, st.st_dev, st.st_ino, typ, st.st_mode & 0o7777, st.st_nlink,
                   st.st_uid, user, st.st_gid, group, getattr(st, "st_rdev", 0), st.st_size,
                   getattr(st, "st_blksize", 4096), getattr(st, "st_blocks", 0),
                   ftime(st.st_atime), ftime(st.st_mtime), ftime(st.st_ctime), None)
            self.last_query = (cols, [row])
        except OSError as e:
            self.last_query = (cols, [(os.path.dirname(path) + "/", os.path.basename(path),
                                       None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None,
                                       None, None, None, None, None, None, None, str(e))])
        if self.current_view() != "db":
            self.view_stack.append("db")
        return True
    return False

Session.exec_sql = _sess_exec_sql
Session._handle_sql_side_effects = _sess_handle_sql_side_effects
Session._try_table_valued = _sess_try_table_valued

            # INSERT/UPDATE etc. Reference: output empty, view? INSERT INTO lnav_example_log gave no output and no db view print.
            # Check if statement is SELECT-like with no description? Keep last_query unchanged, don't switch view.
            # Detect message-style SELECT results: e.g. scripts do ;SELECT 'info: ...' AS msg expecting? rename-stdin script ends with that.
            # But our cur.description would be non-None for SELECT. For UPDATE lnav_file etc, apply side effects:
            self._handle_sql_side_effects(sql_text, exec_sql, params)
            try:
                self.db.commit()
            except Exception:
                pass
    except Exception as e:
        if getattr(self, "_raise_error_msg", None) is not None:
            self.write_err(f"  error: {self._raise_error_msg}\n --> {self.cmd_source}:{self.cmd_index}\n | {pad_cmd_line(orig_cmd)}\n")
            return
        # Table-valued functions fallback: regexp_capture / fstat / xpath
        handled = self._try_table_valued(sql_text, orig_cmd)
        if handled:
            return
        msg = str(e)
        # Normalize some messages to reference wording
        # sqlite python messages are same C messages mostly: 'no such table: foo', 'near "SELEC": syntax error'
        self.write_err(
            f"  error: failed to compile SQL statement\n reason: {msg}\n"
            f" --> {self.cmd_source}:{self.cmd_index}\n | {pad_cmd_line(sql_text.strip())}\n")
        # On SQL error, reference suppresses default view print (OUT empty). Achieve by flag.
        self._sql_error = True
        self._direct_output_done = True  # suppress default print? But multiple commands: later commands may still print.
        # Actually for ";SELECT * FROM foo" with file, OUT was '' (default suppressed). For simplicity suppress if this was last?
        # We'll let driver decide: if any error occurred and view is log, still print? Probe: mark-expr error + write error -> OUT ''.
        # :goto abc error -> OUT ''. So errors generally suppress default output. Track _had_error.
        self._had_error = True

def pragma_table_info(sess, tname):
    # Return reference-style pragma rows
    schema_text = data_text("schema.txt", "")
    tables = parse_schema_columns(schema_text)
    simple = parse_simple_tables(schema_text)
    cols_def = tables.get(tname) or simple.get(tname)
    if cols_def is None:
        # fallback to sqlite pragma
        try:
            cur = sess.db.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({tname})")
            rows = cur.fetchall()
            return ([d[0] for d in cur.description], rows)
        except Exception:
            return (["cid", "name", "type", "notnull", "dflt_value", "pk"], [])
    rows = []
    for i, (col, typ, hidden, pk) in enumerate(cols_def):
        # Visible + hidden interleaved as in schema order; reference PRAGMA truncates after visible+
        # some hidden? Observed syslog PRAGMA output continued past log_annotations (hidden cols follow).
        # Our earlier probe truncated display at 4000 chars, not actual. Include all.
        rows.append((i, col, typ, 0, None, pk))
    return (["cid", "name", "type", "notnull", "dflt_value", "pk"], rows)

def _sess_handle_sql_side_effects(self, OrigSql, exec_sql, params):
    # UPDATE lnav_file SET filepath=... (rename-stdin)
    m = re.match(r"\s*UPDATE\s+lnav_file\s+SET\s+filepath\s*=\s*\?\s+WHERE\s+filepath\s*=\s*'stdin'", exec_sql, re.I)
    if m and params:
        newname = params[0]
        for lf in self.files:
            if lf.filepath == "stdin":
                lf.filepath = str(newname)
        for msg in self.messages:
            if msg.path == "stdin":
                msg.path = str(newname)
        self._populate_db()
    # UPDATE on log tables for log_mark etc: our DB tables are copies; re-sync marks if possible (skip)

def _sess_try_table_valued(self, sql_text, orig_cmd):
    s = sql_text.strip()
    # SELECT * FROM regexp_capture('str', 'pat') [... WHERE etc not supported fully]
    m = re.search(r"regexp_capture\s*\(\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*,\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*\)", s)
    kind = None
    if "regexp_capture(" in s or "regexp_capture_into_json(" in s:
        kind = "regexp_capture"
    elif re.search(r"\bfstat\s*\(", s):
        kind = "fstat"
    if kind == "regexp_capture" and m:
        hay = m.group(1).replace("''", "'")
        pat = m.group(2).replace("''", "'")
        try:
            rx = re.compile(_convert_pattern(pat))
        except Exception:
            return False
        cols = ["match_index", "capture_index", "capture_name", "capture_count", "range_start", "range_stop", "content"]
        rows = []
        for mi, mm in enumerate(rx.finditer(hay)):
            groups = [mm.group(0)] + list(mm.groups())
            spans = [mm.span(0)] + [mm.span(i + 1) for i in range(len(mm.groups()))]
            names = [None]
            inv = {v: k for k, v in rx.groupindex.items()}
            for gi in range(len(mm.groups())):
                names.append(inv.get(gi + 1))
            for ci, (content, (a, b)) in enumerate(zip(groups, spans)):
                rows.append((mi, ci, names[ci] if ci < len(names) else None, len(groups), a + 1, b + 1, content))
        self.last_query = (cols, rows)
        if self.current_view() != "db":
            self.view_stack.append("db")
        self._had_error = False
        self._direct_output_done = False
        return True
    if kind == "fstat":
        m2 = re.search(r"fstat\s*\(\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*\)", s)
        if not m2:
            return False
        path = m2.group(1).replace("''", "'")
        cols = ["st_parent", "st_name", "st_dev", "st_ino", "st_type", "st_mode", "st_nlink",
                "st_uid", "st_user", "st_gid", "st_group", "st_rdev", "st_size", "st_blksize",
                "st_blocks", "st_atime", "st_mtime", "st_ctime", "error"]
        try:
            import pwd, grp
            st = os.stat(path)
            parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)) + "/"
            name = os.path.basename(path)
            typ = "reg" if os.path.isfile(path) else ("dir" if os.path.isdir(path) else "unknown")
            try:
                user = pwd.getpwuid(st.st_uid).pw_name
            except Exception:
                user = str(st.st_uid)
            try:
                group = grp.getgrgid(st.st_gid).gr_name
            except Exception:
                group = str(st.st_gid)
            def ftime(t):
                dt = datetime.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(t)
                return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.") + f"{dt.microsecond:06d}"
            row = (parent, name, st.st_dev, st.st_ino, typ, st.st_mode & 0o7777, st.st_nlink,
                   st.st_uid, user, st.st_gid, group, getattr(st, "st_rdev", 0), st.st_size,
                   getattr(st, "st_blksize", 4096), getattr(st, "st_blocks", 0),
                   ftime(st.st_atime), ftime(st.st_mtime), ftime(st.st_ctime), None)
            self.last_query = (cols, [row])
        except OSError as e:
            self.last_query = (cols, [(os.path.dirname(path) + "/", os.path.basename(path),
                                       None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None,
                                       None, None, None, None, None, None, None, str(e))])
        if self.current_view() != "db":
            self.view_stack.append("db")
        return True
    return False

Session._handle_sql_side_effects = _sess_handle_sql_side_effects
Session._try_table_valued = _sess_try_table_valued

    # full starts with ';'
    sql = full[1:]

def _sess_exec_script_cmd(self, full, orig):
    # full starts with '|': script path/name + args
    rest = full[1:].strip()
    if not rest:
        return
    try:
        tokens = shlex.split(rest)
    except Exception:
        tokens = rest.split()
    if not tokens:
        return
    script_token = tokens[0]
    script_args = tokens[1:]
    # Resolve script: absolute/relative path, or name in formats/default (<name>.lnav) or installed
    script_path = None
    content = None
    if os.path.isfile(script_token):
        script_path = os.path.abspath(script_token)
        try:
            with open(script_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape") as fh:
                content = fh.read()
        except OSError:
            content = None
    else:
        # search home formats/default + installed + data formats
        candidates = [script_token + ".lnav", script_token]
        for cand in candidates:
            data = data_read(f"formats/{cand}")
            if data is not None:
                content = data.decode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
                script_path = os.path.join(home_dir(), "formats/default", cand)
                break
        if content is None:
            # home installed dirs on disk
            for base in (os.path.join(home_dir(), "formats/default"),
                         os.path.join(home_dir(), "formats/installed")):
                for cand in candidates:
                    p = os.path.join(base, cand)
                    if os.path.isfile(p):
                        script_path = p
                        with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape") as fh:
                            content = fh.read()
                        break
                if content is not None:
                    break
    if content is None:
        self.write_err(f"  error: unknown script -- {script_token} -- file not found\n"
                       f" --> {self.cmd_source}:{self.cmd_index}\n | {pad_cmd_line(orig)}\n")
        self._had_error = True
        self._direct_output_done = True
        return
    saved_args = self.script_args
    saved_source = self.cmd_source
    saved_index = self.cmd_index
    self.script_args = script_args
    # Execute lines; multi-line SQL statements in scripts: a ';' line may continue on next lines
    # until next line starting with :, ;, |, #. e.g. rename-stdin has WHERE on second line indented.
    lines = content.splitlines()
    buf = None
    buf_start = 0

    def flush_buf():
        nonlocal buf
        if buf is not None:
            self.cmd_source = script_path or saved_source
            self.cmd_index = buf_start
            # For errors inside scripts referenced via -c '|...', reference shows chained locations:
            # " --> command-option:1\n | |rename-stdin foo\n --> /path/script:7\n | ;SELECT raise_error..."
            # Our exec_sql writes single location (script). To approximate chain for raise_error case,
            # special handling below checks _raise_error. Keep simple for now.
            self.exec_any(buf)
            buf = None
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if buf is not None:
            # continuation if line is indented / doesn't start with command prefix at col0
            if line.startswith((":", ";", "|", "#")) or (line and not line[0].isspace() and line.strip()):
                flush_buf()
            else:
                buf += "\n" + line
                continue
        if buf is None:
            if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
                continue
            buf = line
            buf_start = idx
            # SQL/commands may be single-line; keep buffering to allow continuation lines handling at next iter
            # Flush immediately if next handling... simpler: keep buf and flush on next command line.
            continue
    flush_buf()
    self.script_args = saved_args
    self.cmd_source = saved_source
    self.cmd_index = saved_index

Session.exec_sql_cmd = _sess_exec_sql_cmd
Session.exec_script_cmd = _sess_exec_script_cmd

            return (t, m.path or "", m.line_no)"""
assert old_sortdef in s

p.write_text(s); print("ok")

"""            if m.fmt_name in ("vmw_py_log", "java_log"):
                has_zone = False""",1)
# Spark/HDFS lines wrongly parsed as java messages with bogus times in ours because spark/hdfs regex timestamp groups parse with new formats giving 2026 / 2017. In ref they are java messages but with log_time = max clamp (2025...) - their timestamps apparently failed to parse in ref too (log_time clamped, actual NULL). Our new %y formats make them parse -> different. Remove those two formats (keep %y%m%d %H:%M:%S for mysql abbrev).
s=s.replace(' "%y%m%d %H%M%S", "%d/%m/%y %H:%M:%S", "%y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S",','',1)
# Their sort position via sort_time carry-forward already placed correctly before this change?
